token-counter.assumptionNote: Estimates are a heuristic for English text on GPT-style tokenizers. Exact counts need the model's own tokenizer.
benefits: Instant token estimates for any prompt before you send it.
Helps you stay inside a model's context window.
Plan and trim long prompts without guesswork.
Compare prompt sizes across drafts at a glance.
Private — your prompt text never leaves your browser.

faqs.a: A token is the unit a language model reads and writes — roughly 3/4 of an English word. Models charge per token and have a maximum context window measured in tokens.
Roughly 1 token per 4 characters of English text, or about 0.75 words. This tool averages the character-based and word-based estimates for a stable number.
faqs.q: How many tokens is one word?

faqs.a: The tool uses a published heuristic (about 4 characters per token) and blends it with a word-based estimate. Real tokenizers split text slightly differently, so treat the result as an estimate within about 10 percent.
No. It runs fully in your browser and uses only arithmetic on your text. The 128k reference is just a familiar example of a large context window.
faqs.q: Does it use the official OpenAI tokenizer?

faqs.a: Tokenizers differ by model, but the 4-characters-per-token heuristic works as a rough guide for most English text across GPT, Claude, Gemini and Llama-style models.
faqs.q: Does it work for Claude and Gemini too?

faqs.a: Yes — everything is computed locally. Your prompts are never uploaded or logged.

howTo: Paste your prompt into the text box.
Read the estimated token count instantly.
Check the context percentage to see how much of a 128k window your prompt fills.
Trim or split the prompt if it approaches the model's limit.
Rewrite and re-paste to compare drafts.
keyFacts: Language models read text as tokens, not characters or words.
About 100 tokens is roughly 75 English words.
Token counts decide both cost and whether a prompt fits the context window.
Tokenizers merge common words into single tokens and split rare words into pieces.
Non-English scripts and code can use noticeably more tokens per character.

token-counter.quickAnswer: Estimates how many tokens your prompt will use in a large language model, using a standard client-side heuristic (about 4 characters per token, blended with a word-based estimate). Shows character and word counts too, plus what fraction of a 128k context window the prompt fills — handy before sending long prompts to ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini.
token-counter.tagline: Estimate LLM tokens for any prompt — instant and private.
token-counter.workedExample:
Text: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
Characters: 43
Words: 9
Token estimate: average(43 ÷ 4 = 10.75, 9 × 1.33 = 11.97) ≈ 11 tokens
Context: 11 ÷ 128000 × 100 ≈ 0.01% of a 128k window
